transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I came in today because... well, the thought of getting on an airplane right now just scares me so bad. I know it doesn't make any sense, but my body just tells me that the plane is going to fall. It's gotten really hard to deal with.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things in your life on most days, or is your anxiety primarily focused on the fear of flying?

No, it's really just the flying. I mean, I have the normal stress that comes with work and life, but I don't worry about things all the time. It's just... when it comes to airplanes, that's when the panic hits me. It's completely focused on that one thing.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denied excessive worrying about many different things, which rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). The fear is specifically focused on flying, which is a situational specific phobia, ruling out F40.231 (fear of blood/injections).
